name: Chinese Numerals
morphology: Chinese numerals combine digits (一–九) with units (十, 百, 千, 萬, 億) through multiplicative compounding.
context: Chinese numerals formed one of the earliest numeric systems and are used today in finance and official documents.
rules: Chinese numerals combine digits (一 to 九) with units (十, 百, 千, 萬, 億).
If a unit appears alone, it implies one of that unit (十 = 10).
零 marks internal gaps (105 = 一百零五).
No subtractive notation exists; all values are additive.
